prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on what matters to you (price, lifetime warranty, storm/insurance experience, speed, metal vs shingle, etc.). A quick way forward: tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an insurance claim, and I’ll tailor recommendations. Meanwhile, here’s a concise guide you can use right away to find the best roofer in Dallas.

Key questions to decide “best”
- Is this an insurance claim (storm damage) or a homeowner-pay replacement?
- Roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile) and size/complexity?
- Budget vs. desire for highest-grade materials and long warranties?
- How quickly do you need it done?

How to pick the best Dallas roofer (step-by-step)
1. Get at least 3 written estimates. Compare scope of work, materials, ventilation, decking repair, and removal vs overlay.
2. Verify credentials
   - Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred). These show training and warranty options.
   - Proof of general liability and workers’ comp insurance.
   - Local business registration and any city permits (Dallas requires permits for roof work).
   - Check BBB rating and Google/Angi/Yelp reviews and recent photos.
3. Ask these essential questions
   - Exact materials brand, model, warranty (manufacturer vs workmanship) and who backs the workmanship warranty.
   - Start/end dates, daily cleanup plan, and how they protect landscaping.
   - How they handle unseen deck/structural repairs and change orders.
   - Will they obtain permits and arrange inspections?
   - Do they have a local office and show recent local references?
4. Red flags
   - Demand for full payment upfront or very low bid far below competitors.
   - No written contract or vague warranty language.
   - Uses only subcontractors with no company oversight (or won’t name them).
5. Storm/insurance tips
   - Ask whether they will work directly with your insurer and provide Xactimate-style estimates.
   - Beware of contractors pressuring you to sign assignment-of-benefits; know your rights first.
6. Material and workmanship warranty nuances
   - Manufacturer warranty covers shingles; workmanship (installation) warranty is separate. Get both in writing.
   - For hail-prone Dallas area, ask about Class 4 impact-rated shingles and storm warranties.
7. After hire
   - Keep all invoices, permits, photos, and the contract.
   - Final payment only after satisfied completion and final inspection.

If you want, give me:
- Your Dallas ZIP code
- Roof type and whether insurance is involved
I’ll suggest several Dallas-area contractors (highly rated options and what to check specifically for each) and a sample question list tailored to your situation.
